title: The Feud over Lactate and Its Role in Brain Energy Metabolism and Beyond: An Unnecessary Burden on Research and the Scientists Who Practice It
content: Ever since the monocarboxylate, lactate, was shown to be more than a useless end-product of anaerobic glycolysis, the members of the brain energy metabolism research community are divided by two issues: First, could lactate replace glucose as the oxidative mitochondrial energy substrate? Second, should glycolysis continue to be divided into aerobic and anaerobic pathways? This review examines both the history and the reasons for this division and offers a unifying solution.
